The organic electroluminescence device includes a base material provided with a recessed portion, and a light emitting element formed in association with the recessed portion. A reflective layer is disposed on the recessed portion of the base material, and a transparent filling layer is provided over the reflective layer so as to fill at least part of the recess.

Above the transparent filling layer, a transparent first electrode, an organic light emitting layer, and a transparent second electrode are sequentially stacked. These layers together form the light emitting element, in which light generated by the organic light emitting layer can be emitted through the transparent electrodes. The reflective layer positioned beneath the filling layer reflects light toward the emission side, thereby improving light extraction efficiency.

The display region of the organic electroluminescence device is divided into a plurality of separated unit regions. Each unit region includes a light emitting area and a non-emissive area. The light emitting area contains the light emitting element described above, while the non-emissive area contains a light absorption layer. The light absorption layer suppresses unwanted reflection or stray light in the non-emissive area, thereby enhancing display contrast and improving the visual quality of the device.
outputs.L4:
An organic electroluminescence display device is provided in which a plurality of display unit regions are defined on a substrate. Each display unit region includes one or more light-emitting elements formed in recessed base regions, so that the position and optical behavior of each emitting area can be precisely controlled. The recessed regions are provided with filling layers that may include reflective portions and transparent portions. The reflective filling layers are arranged to reflect light generated by the organic light-emitting layer toward the viewing side of the device, while the transparent filling layers allow light to pass through without substantial loss. By combining these layers with transparent electrodes, the device efficiently extracts light from selected regions and forms a well-defined display pattern.

Each light-emitting element includes a transparent electrode, an organic electroluminescent layer, and an opposing electrode. When a voltage is applied between the electrodes, the organic light-emitting layer emits light. The emitted light is guided and controlled by the structure of the recessed base region and the optical characteristics of the filling layers. In particular, reflective layers positioned below or around the emitting region help redirect light that would otherwise be lost, thereby increasing brightness and improving viewing efficiency. The transparent electrode allows the generated light to exit through the intended display surface.

The display surface is divided into a plurality of unit regions, and each unit region is further separated into an emissive area and a non-emissive area. The emissive area contains the organic electroluminescence element and is responsible for producing visible light. The non-emissive area does not generate display light and may include wiring, drive elements, separation structures, or other functional components required for operation of the display. To prevent unwanted reflection or scattering from these non-emissive areas, a light absorption layer is provided in at least part of the non-emissive region.

The light absorption layer absorbs stray light, ambient light, and light leaking from adjacent emissive areas. This reduces optical interference between neighboring display elements and suppresses the appearance of unwanted brightness in regions that are intended to remain dark. As a result, the contrast ratio of the display is improved, black levels are enhanced, and the boundaries between display pixels or subpixels become clearer. The arrangement also helps reduce glare caused by external light reflection.

By using recessed base regions, transparent electrodes, reflective and transparent filling layers, and non-emissive light absorption regions, the organic electroluminescence device achieves controlled light emission and improved display quality. The structure enables efficient use of generated light while minimizing stray light and optical crosstalk. Accordingly, the device is suitable for high-performance flat-panel displays requiring high brightness, high contrast, and accurately defined light-emitting regions.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” may be one of the smallest words in the English language, but it plays a very important role. It is known as the definite article, and it helps us talk about specific people, places, things, or ideas. For example, when we say “the book,” we are not talking about just any book—we mean a particular book that the speaker and listener both understand.

This simple word brings clarity to communication. It helps identify what is already known, what is unique, or what has been mentioned before. We say “the sun” because there is only one sun in our sky, and we say “the teacher” when we know which teacher is being discussed.

Although “the” is often overlooked, it appears constantly in everyday speech and writing. It connects ideas, gives meaning to sentences, and makes language more precise. Without “the,” English would feel less natural and much harder to understand.

In short, “the” is a small word with a big purpose. It shows that even the simplest parts of language can be essential.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract describing an organic electroluminescence device with a recessed base, reflective layer, transparent filling layer, transparent electrodes, organic light emitting layer, divided display regions, and light absorption layer in non-emissive areas.
counterfactuals.output: An organic electroluminescence device includes a base having a recess corresponding to a display area, a reflective layer disposed in the recess, and a transparent filling layer provided over the reflective layer so as to planarize the recess. A plurality of transparent electrodes is arranged on or above the transparent filling layer, and an organic light emitting layer is provided in electrical association with the transparent electrodes to emit light toward a viewing side and toward the reflective layer. The display area is divided into a plurality of display regions, each including an emissive area in which light is generated and output, and a non-emissive area between adjacent emissive areas. The reflective layer reflects light emitted from the organic light emitting layer toward the viewing side, thereby improving light extraction efficiency. A light absorption layer is disposed in the non-emissive areas, at least between adjacent display regions, to absorb stray light and suppress optical crosstalk and external light reflection. The transparent filling layer electrically and optically separates the reflective layer from the transparent electrodes while maintaining a substantially flat element-forming surface.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the invention of an organic EL device having a base material with recessed portions, reflective layers inside the recesses, transparent filling material, transparent electrodes, and an organic light-emitting stack.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention describes an organic electroluminescent (EL) device designed to improve light extraction and display performance.

It uses a base material formed with recessed portions. Reflective layers are provided inside these recesses, and the recesses are filled with a transparent filling material so that the surface can be made substantially flat. Over this structure, transparent electrodes are formed, and an organic light-emitting stack is provided as the emission layer structure.

When the organic EL stack emits light, light traveling toward the base side can be reflected by the reflective layers in the recessed portions and redirected outward. The transparent filling material and transparent electrodes allow the emitted and reflected light to pass through efficiently. By arranging reflective regions in the recesses while maintaining a flat device surface, the structure can enhance light utilization, improve brightness, and support stable fabrication of the organic EL layers.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a patent abstract for a transparent organic electroluminescence display that uses recessed reflective cavities for light emitting elements and includes separated unit regions with light absorption layers outside the emitting areas.
counterfactuals.output: A transparent organic electroluminescence display includes a transparent substrate divided into a plurality of unit regions, each unit region including an emission area and a transmission area. A recessed reflective cavity is formed in correspondence with each emission area, and a light emitting element, including an organic emission layer between first and second electrodes, is disposed in the recessed reflective cavity such that light generated by the light emitting element is reflected and directed toward a display side. The recessed reflective cavity may include inclined or curved reflective sidewalls to improve light extraction and reduce optical loss. A light absorption layer is disposed in each unit region outside the emission area, including at least a portion of the transmission area or a non-emission area, and is separated between adjacent unit regions. The separated light absorption layers suppress reflected external light, optical interference, and color mixing while maintaining transparency of the display. Accordingly, the display provides improved emission efficiency, contrast, and visibility while preserving transparent display characteristics.
